images.text: In any organization, managers are said to perform many tasks and play many roles. It is understood that they are responsible for handling challenging and varied situations. When it comes to effectively handling these situations, each manager employs their own management style. Some management styles should be used in some situations and some had better not be used in others. There are four main management styles considered to be practiced by managers in every industry.

Autocratic
In the autocratic style, the manager is understood to be the sole decision-maker and decisions made reflect the manager's opinion and personality. The team's collective opinion is not generally considered. If the manager has lots of experience, knowledge and exposure, the decisions made by him or her may be better and be reached faster than with collective decision-making.

Democratic
The democratic style means that the manager considers others' opinions and welcomes their contribution to the discussion. Every decision is made with the agreement of the majority and reflects the team's opinion. If this management style is going to work successfully, there had better be robust communication between the team and management. Democratic management is most successful for decision-making when it's a complex matter. Before a decision is made, usually a number of meetings take place. These meetings had better be carefully planned and details should be documented. This style of management usually results in more employee satisfaction because of the collective nature of the process.

Paternalistic
This is considered to be a dictatorial type of management. Decisions are made by the manager in the best interest of the company and its employees. This decision is then explained to the employees and generally receives their support. In this management style, a work-life balance is emphasized and the focus is on maintaining high morale in the office.

Laissez-faire
With laissez-faire management, the manager is a facilitator for staff decision-making. The employees take responsibility for their own work and make many decisions without waiting for management approval. When an employee faces an obstacle, the manager had better intervene and help the employee overcome it. In this style of management the employee is observed to be more independent and owning their decisions and the consequences.

Report Verbs with Impersonal Passive Constructions
When you want to avoid saying the generalized agent (they, people, everybody, etc.) of an action, you can use report verbs such as claim, mention, request, and point out with a passive structure.
You can use the structure: subject + passive reporting verb + to-infinitive

In this pattern you start with the subject of the reported clause (my brother), which is followed by the passive reporting verb (known) and the to-infinitive form of the verb (to like) in the reported clause.

Everybody knows that my brother likes watching football =
My brother is known to like watching football.
Notice that the reporting verb (to know) is in the same tense (present) in both sentences.

Modals for Expressing Duty and Advice: Had Better
You can use the modal phrase had better to express what is the best thing to do in a particular situation.
You're very busy. You had better ask for some help in order to complete your assignment on time.
Had better is stronger in meaning than should/ought to, but it is not as strong as must.
The negative is had better not.
We'd better not delay the delivery of this project.
